chunks: And from him, from Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, who said:

I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about a man who performed 'Umrat al-Tamattu' (the enjoyment of 'Umra until Hajj), so he entered Mecca, performed Tawaf and Sa'i, put on his clothes, and became free from Ihram, but he forgot to shorten his prayer until he went out to Arafat. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no harm with him; he builds upon his 'Umra and its Tawaf, and the Tawaf of Hajj follows after it.'

key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: Arafat (the plain of Arafat, site of Wuquf)
key_terms.يُقَصِّرَ: Qasr (shortening the four-rak'ah prayer to two)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim forgets to shorten prayers during Umrat al-Tamattu?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the ruling for a Mu'tamir who forgets to shorten their prayers after completing the 'Umrah rites but before entering the state of Ihram for Hajj at Arafat. The Imam affirms that the Hajj remains valid by 'building' upon the completed 'Umrah, with the Hajj Tawaf performed immediately after, demonstrating the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding minor omissions during the transition between rituals. This highlights the principle that the validity of the Hajj is not contingent upon the strict sequential perfection of every preparatory act if the core intention and major rites are preserved.
